content: The clinical significance of these findings remains undetermined. Pharmacokinetics Due to the gradual absorption of albuterol from the bronchi, systemic levels of the drug are low following inhalation of recommended doses. Studies conducted on four subjects who were administered tritiated albuterol showed that maximum plasma concentrations occurred within two to four hours. However, the sensitivity of the assay method used in these studies was insufficient to determine the metabolic rate and plasma elimination half-life of albuterol. Approximately 72% of the inhaled dose is excreted in the urine within 24 hours, with 28% excreted as unchanged drug and 44% as metabolites. In animal studies, albuterol sulfate was evaluated for its safety profile. In one study, dietary doses of 0, 10, and 50 mg/kg (equivalent to approximately 15, 70, and 340 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for adults on a mg/m² basis, or approximately 6, 30, and 160 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for children on a mg/m² basis) were administered. The effects of albuterol were blocked when propranolol, a non-selective beta-adrenergic antagonist, was co-administered. In an 18-month study in CD-1 mice, albuterol sulfate showed no evidence of tumorigenicity at dietary doses of up to 500 mg/kg (approximately 1700 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for adults on a mg/m² basis, or approximately 800 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for children on a mg/m² basis). Similarly, in a 22-month study in Golden hamsters, no evidence of tumorigenicity was observed at dietary doses of up to 50 mg/kg (approximately 225 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for adults on a mg/m² basis, or approximately 110 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for children on a mg/m² basis). Albuterol sulfate was not mutagenic in the Ames test, with or without metabolic activation, using tester strains Salmonella typhimurium TA1537, TA1538, and TA98, or Escherichia coli WP2, WP2uvrA, and WP67. No forward mutations were observed in yeast strain Saccharomyces cerevisiae S9, nor was there any mitotic gene conversion in yeast strain S. cerevisiae JD1, with or without metabolic activation. Fluctuation assays in E. coli WP2, both with and without metabolic activation, were negative. Albuterol sulfate was not clastogenic in a human peripheral lymphocyte assay or in an AH1 strain mouse micronucleus assay at intraperitoneal doses of up to 200 mg/kg. Reproductive studies in rats demonstrated no evidence of impaired fertility at oral doses of up to 50 mg/kg (approximately 340 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for adults on a mg/m² basis). Clinical Studies In controlled clinical trials involving adults with asthma, the onset of improvement in pulmonary function was observed within 15 minutes, as measured by both maximum midexpiratory flow rate (MMEF) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1). MMEF measurements indicated that near-maximum improvement in pulmonary function generally occurred within 60 to 90 minutes following two inhalations of albuterol. Clinically significant improvement typically persisted for three to four hours in most patients, with some patients maintaining a therapeutic response (defined as FEV1 values 15% or more above baseline) for up to six hours. Continued effectiveness of albuterol was demonstrated over a 13-week period in these trials. In controlled clinical trials involving children aged 4 to 12 years, FEV1 measurements showed that maximum improvement in pulmonary function occurred within 30 to 60 minutes. Clinically significant improvement (≥15% increase in FEV1) was observed as early as five minutes following administration of 180 mcg of albuterol in 60% of children in a dose-ranging study. Clinically significant improvement in FEV1 persisted in the majority of patients for two hours and in 33% to 47% of patients for four hours among 56 pediatric patients receiving inhalation aerosol in one study. In a second study involving 48 pediatric patients, clinically significant improvement persisted in the majority for up to one hour and in 23% to 40% for four hours. Additionally, at least 50% of the patients in both studies achieved an improvement in forced expiratory flow rate between 25% and 75% of the forced vital capacity (FEF25%-75%) of at least 20% for two to five hours. Continued effectiveness of albuterol was demonstrated over the 12-week study period. In other clinical studies involving both adults and children, two inhalations of albuterol aerosol taken approximately 15 minutes before exercise effectively prevented exercise-induced bronchospasm. This was demonstrated by the maintenance of FEV1 within 80% of baseline values in the majority of patients. One study in adults also evaluated the duration of the prophylactic effect against repeated exercise challenges, which was evident at four hours in the majority of patients and at six hours in approximately one-third of the patients. How Supplied Albuterol Inhalation Aerosol is supplied in 17 g canisters containing 200 metered inhalations (NDC 17270-721-01) in boxes of one. Each actuation delivers 100 mcg of albuterol from the valve and 90 mcg of albuterol from the mouthpiece.
